name: VidVerge
description: VidVerge brings two focused video workflows together: create polished product videos or enhance footage you already have.

apps.name: Product Video
apps.description: Opens on the Ad Director tab — a full AI Product Advertisement Director: paste a website URL (optionally add real screenshots, a goal and a voice), answer one question — How do you want your product video to feel? Story-Driven (more AI-generated video, minimal motion graphics: cinematic storytelling where graphics are reserved for accurate information — numbers, statistics, pricing, product names, feature names, CTA, URLs, comparisons, precise diagrams) or Product-Focused (the product stays at the center with real UI, screenshots, feature graphics and demonstrations; AI video supports the problem, use case and outcome) — and one click runs the whole production with Claude Opus 5 as the single director brain. The style persists with the project and can be switched later: the storyboard re-plans and every finished clip whose treatment is unchanged is reused, so only redesigned scenes regenerate. It researches the product from the real website and screenshots (extracting the problem, features, benefits, pricing and CTA — never inventing features, pricing, testimonials or statistics), decides the ad strategy (problem / outcome / curiosity / demo hook plus an adapted HOOK→PROBLEM→AGITATION→SOLUTION→DEMO→MECHANISM→FEATURES→BENEFIT→PROOF→CTA structure), writes the complete scene-by-scene voiceover script FIRST, records real TTS audio per scene (ElevenLabs workspace voices with a tts-1 fallback) and measures it so every visual's duration is DERIVED from the voice timing — never arbitrary fixed lengths. It then storyboards the most understandable visual per line from 14 visual types (TEXT, PRODUCT_UI, UI_ANIMATION, AI_VIDEO, B_ROLL, IMAGE, MOTION_GRAPHIC, EDUCATIONAL_DIAGRAM, COMPARISON, PROCESS, TIMELINE, BEFORE_AFTER, PRODUCT_MOCKUP, SPLIT_SCREEN): real-screenshot device mockups with an animated travelling cursor, clicks, typing carets and callout labels for anything UI (generative video is never asked to recreate an interface — the crawler even captures a real website screenshot when none is uploaded), Google Omni Flash generative video strictly for B-roll/lifestyle/cinematic moments with the narration context baked into every production prompt and frame-chained continuity, GSAP + SVG motion graphics and educational diagrams that explain relationships and processes (INPUT → ANALYSIS → RESULT with animated arrows — never random floating word cards; on-screen text is minimal support, never the visual), and generated images with optional Omni image-to-video animation. Every render is Opus-inspected against its narration and storyboard intent with up to two automatic fix retakes, and QA never trusts the plan or prompt — the actual rendered file is the source of truth: each scene stores a required-content manifest at storyboard time, every rendered file is validated as a real, decodable, non-blank video (an API returning a URL is never success; blank AI videos fail and retake), frames extracted from the actual render are checked with OCR + vision against the manifest (required exact text must actually be readable; exact text on AI-video scenes renders as a deterministic SVG overlay composited over the footage, never left to the generative model), a final seven-point quality-control pass (generic visual, too much text, unclear explanation, fake UI, poor pacing, missing dialogue sync, weak CTA) regenerates only the weak scenes, and FFmpeg composes the final MP4 in-browser: per-scene voice mixed into its own segment with native footage audio ducked underneath, auto-generated captions from the actual voiceover transcript with smart line breaks and keyword emphasis, an ElevenLabs music bed chosen by strategy (energetic startup / modern tech / cinematic / minimal / premium) auto-ducked under narration, and an optional subtle SFX bed — then a FINAL-VIDEO QA re-inspects the actual composed MP4 per scene time-window (frame extraction + OCR + vision + blank-frame sweep + narration-audio check), catching overlays that vanish during composition, and the ad is only marked ready when it passes; any failure explains itself with expected / detected / cause / fix. The studio shows URL input → live analysis → the strategy summary → the script preview → the scene-by-scene storyboard where every card carries its narration line, visual-type badge, preview frame, voice-derived duration and status with Retake / Retake-with-note / Edit-narration (re-voiced, re-timed, re-rendered) / Swap-visual-type (Opus redesigns the scene for the new type) controls, plus a voice-timed timeline preview and export. After the main ad, one click has Opus plan AD VARIATIONS — different hook (a newly generated opening scene), faster cut, more cinematic, more educational, short social cut — each reusing the already-generated scenes and composing its own downloadable MP4. Auto Generate and Auto Mix are ON by default and user-switchable (Auto Generate off pauses after the storyboard until a Generate scenes click; Auto Mix off composes with narration only); an edited prompt is stored as a persistent override and used verbatim — never silently replaced by the director (a YOUR PROMPT badge marks the scene, Reset prompt returns to the AI prompt); GSAP capture is the default graphics engine with Remotion available as an opt-in secondary engine for complex frame-accurate compositions (same normalized scene spec, automatic GSAP fallback); every stage persists and resumes after reloads, and a background worker adopts finished renders and fails dead operations every ~15 minutes even while the tab is closed — no run sits at GENERATING forever. All previous flows remain one tab away: Track B: designed product films built with HyperFrames from your real product. Scenes made from real product screenshots render with the premium SaaS-demo treatment: cinematic establishing/close-up/return camera moves with eased pushes, an animated demo cursor that travels to UI regions and clicks, types, toggles or scrolls (press, ripple and caret effects — never teleporting), spotlight/outline feature highlights with background dimming, timeline-synced caption pills, chained camera/expand/focus scene transitions, and UI sound effects on the clicks and cuts — all driven by one deterministic per-scene timeline (retime a scene and its camera, cursor, highlights, captions and SFX retime together), responsive to 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 framing. Lands on a My Videos gallery of 3D cards, then a full-screen agentic editor — live-autosaved text, timing, music, brand colours, drag-to-reorder scenes, credit-gated regeneration, and an 'Ask AI to edit' bar. Creation offers a Choose Style step with six options: the standard HyperFrames Product Launch film, plus five styled pipelines (Clip Style hand-cut paper collage, Cinematic Trailer, Text-to-Video (English) generated straight from a typed description, Documentary, Product Showcase), each with its own script strategy, image strategy, motion parameters and musical register. A styled pick opens a guided seven-step flow: style, product or typed description, length (which sets the scene budget), the SCRIPT REVIEW GATE where Claude writes a hook plus per-scene visual directions plus a call to action and nothing renders until the customer approves it, the frame prompts, the ElevenLabs sound (narration voiceover, background music, an optional sound-effects brief and an optional captions toggle, all previewable first), then generate. The server pipeline renders every shot, joins them, and lays the narration, music, sound effects and optional burned-in captions over the film in a final pass, with a .SRT caption file alongside. A Saved Videos tab is the unified, self-healing gallery of every finished video from both flows, persisted in the database; a Product Launch film gets the same sound and captions step from a Sound button on its card. Once initiated, the production pipeline self-drives to completion in the background — a 5-minute server sweep adopts finished renders and submits the next shot even with the tab closed. A separate Design with AI tab designs motion graphics onto a video the customer already has (typically a talking-head video): upload the video (up to 500MB, the original is never modified), auto-generate a word-timestamped transcript or import an SRT/VTT to skip retranscription (editable, SRT export), optionally set a visual style (Auto Brand / Minimal / Cinematic), a product URL for brand context and real screenshots — then one Design My Video click has Claude Opus 5 detect the talking-head position (graphics never cover the face), read the transcript, and design per-timestamp compositable overlay graphics — icons, animated diagrams, charts, stats, callout arrows, step flows, checklists, comparisons, progress bars, kinetic typography, lower thirds and real-screenshot cards, all deterministic GSAP + SVG (graphics-first, minimal text, no Remotion), plus real AI-footage cutaways (Omni) reserved for the few moments that genuinely need actual video — through Generating Visual Plan → Creating Graphics → Syncing to Transcript → an agentic Quality Check that inspects composited frames and fixes only flagged graphics. The result opens as a live preview (original video + overlays seeked in real time, no render wait) over an editable timeline where each graphic is independently movable, resizable, repositionable, restylable, duplicatable, deletable and AI-regenerable, with whole-design controls (Regenerate / More Dynamic / More Minimal / More Product-Focused / More Cinematic / More Professional / Change Brand Style, talking-head layout, density) — and Export composites everything in-browser and encodes a downloadable MP4 with FFmpeg. Runs persist per stage and resume after reloads.

apps.name: Video Enhancer
apps.description: Full AI editing suite for footage you already have, in a dark editor around a centered preview. Analyze: an AI vision model watches sampled frames, reports smart findings (a supporting chart appears only when a finding carries a score, comparison, recommendation or multi-step explanation — plain findings stay text) and designs adaptive graphic overlays for that exact content — motion-path arrows, callouts with leader lines, numbered step badges, pulsing highlight rings, labels and mini flow diagrams (strictly graphics, never captions), each previewing live, color-coded, toggleable and click-to-seek. Full toolset: trim/cut with draggable in/out timeline handles, split-at-playhead and per-segment keep/cut; brightness/contrast/saturation/blur/vignette filters plus 0.5×–2× speed; draggable timed text overlays with size, color and duration; Auto Captions that transcribe the footage's own audio (word-timed) and render synced captions in four styles — Brand (VidVerge charcoal pill, warm white text, coral word-highlight, the default), Bold Pop, Karaoke and Minimal — with a master on/off toggle, per-line edit/delete and a caption position control (top, middle or bottom), shown live on the preview and burned into the export; 16:9, 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5 aspect presets as a centered cover-crop; original-audio mute/volume; an ElevenLabs music bed from a mood prompt, a preset style or an auto-suggested mood matched to the footage, with a music-vs-original volume slider; and a Sound FX library (applause, whoosh, notification, chime, camera shutter, pop, riser, drum hit, sparkle, rain, city and bird ambience, or a custom typed description) dropped at the playhead with its own volume, mixed alongside the original audio and music (music and sound effects use the founder's ELEVENLABS_API_KEY when configured, built-in engine otherwise). Effects include gradient and solid backdrop framing plus a background-softening focus mode. Export composites the whole edit — including captions and sound effects — in one pass into a downloadable MP4 (or WebM) with High/Standard/Compact quality options; the output is stored durably and replaces the raw upload in the player with a View-original toggle. Also the handoff target for SceneForge: a finished SceneForge video opened "in the Editor" or "sent to the Enhancer" loads here automatically, ready to trim, overlay, caption, add sound, rescore or enhance.

apps.name: Script-to-Video
apps.description: The rebuilt script-to-film pipeline with Claude Opus 5 as the single director brain: paste a script (never rewritten) and Opus breaks it into independent scenes, deciding per scene how it gets made — cinematic live-action shots on Veo (with a hard rule against on-screen text), deterministic motion graphics rendered in the browser with HTML/SVG + GSAP (eleven varied treatments — kinetic type, documentary lower-thirds, flowcharts, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, timelines, comparisons, node maps, quotes, annotated images — each with its own content-matched palette, never a repeated generic card), real product screenshots inside animated phone/laptop/browser mockups (Veo is never asked to recreate a UI), and reused project assets with cinematic motion and exact labels. Continuity is frame-chained: after each Veo scene the last frame is extracted and Opus reads its visual attributes (lighting, character, environment, camera) into the next scene's prompt, so consecutive cinematic shots carry the same person, place and light; independent scenes render in parallel. After every render Opus checks the clip against its script segment and flags mismatches. Every scene is independent — own spec, status, cached clip — so regenerating one scene never touches the rest, and a docked Director bar revises any single scene from a plain-English note. Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser: normalization, audio handling and the final MP4 cut, no server renderer. On the Final screen, an opt-in Finish step can add ElevenLabs narration from the untouched original script, an ElevenLabs music bed automatically ducked beneath narration and native scene sound, and scene-timed burned-in captions built from each stored script segment and measured duration; generated tracks and settings are persisted and reused. Runs persist to the database at every step and resume after reloads. Legacy projects stay watchable in the Library.

apps.name: SceneForge
apps.description: SceneForge v4 is a talking-head + documentary motion-graphics studio: the HeyGen avatar master carries the film (intro, transitions and CTA on camera) while MIDDLE VISUAL SECTIONS cut in over its picture and the presenter's narration keeps playing underneath, documentary style. The single orchestrator LLM writes the script, then produces a full video blueprint: every middle scene gets a customer-switchable type — AI VIDEO (real generated footage on Gemini Omni Flash; an unchanged prompt reuses its clip), MOTION GRAPHIC (the new GSAP + SVG engine: branching diagrams, flowcharts, timelines, comparisons, list reveals, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, node graphs, annotated images and text reveals, all rendered from a structured spec whose every string and number appears EXACTLY as written — important text never goes inside AI video; scenes preview live in the browser and are captured with MediaRecorder into real video clips), IMAGE (one strong Omni Flash still), or TEXT OVERLAY (a deterministic animated headline captured the same way). The blueprint timeline is colour-coded: HeyGen blue, AI video purple, motion graphics green, images orange, text teal. Scenes are independently editable — switching a type or editing a spec regenerates ONLY that scene, every clip is cached, re-assembly never re-renders finished scenes, and the HeyGen master stays locked unless explicitly re-recorded. Final assembly composites the middle clips over the continuous avatar master: 9:16 films run through the platform's server-side FFmpeg overlay compositor (base narration audio kept uninterrupted), 16:9 films use one deterministic compositing render because the platform's FFmpeg compositor is portrait-only today. Steps: topic → deep-research script → live HeyGen v3 avatar render (resumable after reload) → style → blueprint review with live GSAP previews and per-scene capture → parallel middle-visual production with per-scene Retry / switch type / Skip → audio-preserving assembly, six quality checks, inline player, ElevenLabs music bed under a 16:9 master → editor handoff — plus the built-in Asset Studio (Omni Flash stills attached straight onto scenes, always reused, never re-billed) and natural-language script/scene/style/assembly changes via Verger.

apps.name: Ads Studio
apps.description: Agentic short-form ad engine: product URL + avatar + assets in, a finished professional ad out. A linear 8-step workflow (Product → Research → Angles → Script → Scene Plan → Generate → Review → Variations) with Claude Opus 5 as the single creative brain. Research crawls the product site (plus /reviews, /testimonials, /pricing and /about) and extracts a structured direct-response brief — features, pricing, pain points, desires, objections, mechanism, awareness level and real customer language, each marked [VERIFIED] or [INFERRED], never invented — that the user can correct inline. Opus then generates 8–12 genuinely different ad angles (selectable cards with an 'Opus picks best' judge), writes a 4–7 clip script (Hook → Problem → Agitate → Solution → Proof → Benefit → single CTA) under hard per-duration word limits (4s→9, 6s→13, 8s→17, 10s→22 words) with live word-count validation and per-clip duration selectors, and directs a full per-clip scene plan — camera, framing, micro-action, gesture, expression, environment, lighting, ONE locked voice description reused verbatim across all clips, continuity notes, overlay plan and an assembled production Veo prompt (clip 1 must open on a first-second pattern interrupt, never a static talking head). Generation is an agentic loop: each clip renders on the platform video model with the uploaded avatar as the character reference, Opus vision inspects the take against the plan (action, framing, flow, same character, clutter, composition), a rejected take auto-regenerates ONCE with the inspector's adjusted prompt (max 2 attempts), and the final frame of each clip is read by Opus into the next clip's continuity clause. Real screenshots are never recreated by the video model — they composite AFTER generation inside GSAP-animated phone/laptop/browser/tablet/monitor mockups, alongside kinetic text callouts, review cards, animated stat counters, CTA buttons, arrow highlights, a logo watermark and styled burned-in captions of each spoken line (all GSAP + SVG rendered to canvas, no Remotion). Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser — chroma-keyed overlay compositing, normalization, concat, faststart MP4 — with a progress bar, a collapsible FFmpeg debug log and a download button. A Variations step has Opus write alternative hooks, bodies and CTAs (up to 3×2×2 = 12 combinations); building a variation reuses every clip whose line is unchanged and regenerates only the clips whose spoken line differs, then re-assembles, each with its own download. The session persists to localStorage, so a refresh resumes mid-run. Standalone — shares nothing with Product Video, SceneForge, Video Enhancer or Script-to-Video.
